---
title: "Commands"
---

Three commands.

## `name`

Estimates the gender of one name and says which rule decided.

```bash
icename-gender name "Helga Ingimundardóttir"
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FULL_NAME` | The full name, quoted. |
| `--detail` | Also show what each part of the name says, and the agreement. |
| `--register` | A register CSV to use instead of the bundled snapshot. |

Prints the gender (or `unknown`), a tab, and the rule (or `-`). For the `given_name` rule, the
name that decided follows in brackets.

## `csv`

Adds `gender` and `gender_rule` columns to a CSV of names.

```bash
icename-gender csv people.csv --column name -o people_gender.csv
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `INPUT_PATH` | A UTF-8 CSV with a header row. |
| `--column`, `-c` | The column holding the full names. Default `name`. |
| `--output`, `-o` | Where to write. Default: standard output. |
| `--detail` | Also add `gender_agreement`, `gender_female` and `gender_male`. |
| `--register` | A register CSV to use instead of the bundled snapshot. |

All input columns are kept, in order. An empty cell or an undecided name gets empty
`gender` and `gender_rule`. A count of the results is printed to standard error.

## `registry-fetch`

Fetches the whole register from island.is.

```bash
icename-gender registry-fetch -o mannanafnaskra.csv
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--output`, `-o` | Where to write the register. Default `mannanafnaskra.csv`. |

About 30 requests, under a minute. See [The register](register.qmd).
